title: INTERIM REPORT on the proposal for a Council regulation laying down the Multiannual Financial Framework for the years 2028 to 2034
part_text: 55b. Stresses that digital justice cannot function without robust cybersecurity; notes the growing exposure of judicial and cross-border cooperation systems to cyberthreats; calls for dedicated, ring-fenced resources to ensure secure infrastructure, continuous threat monitoring and effective incident response; underlines that cybersecurity is essential for preserving judicial independence, data integrity and trust in digital justice; calls for mandatory compliance with the network and information systems (NIS) standards set by the NIS2 Directive1a; invites the Commission, furthermore, to ensure coordinated monitoring, threat intelligence and rapid response capacity; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ 1a Directive (EU) 2022/2555 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union, amending Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 and Directive (EU) 2018/1972, and repealing Directive (EU) 2016/1148 (NIS 2 Directive) (OJ L 333, 27.12.2022, p. 8, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2555/oj).
